questions.q: How do fascist movements often first reach power, according to lesson 1?
a: They win elections by democratic means, then work to end democracy
They seize control through immediate military coups
They are appointed by foreign governments to restore order
They take over only after every other party has collapsed
questions.why: Lesson 1 says such parties follow democratic rules at first and turn on them later.

questions.q: Why does the summary say fascism keeps returning throughout history?
a: It speaks to frustrated people who want someone to blame
It offers the most efficient form of government available
It is spread mainly by a small group of secret plotters
It becomes popular only when economies are thriving
questions.why: Lesson 2 says extreme ideologies appear whenever people are deeply frustrated.

questions.q: What did Mussolini compare taking power to?
a: Quietly plucking a live chicken without being noticed
Slowly building a house one brick at a time
Leading a herd of sheep across a narrow bridge
Lighting a fire that no one can put out
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses the image to show that power is taken quietly before anyone reacts.

questions.q: Which modern development does lesson 3 say makes manipulation easier?
a: Disinformation spreading quickly through social media
The decline of newspapers and printed books
The growing number of university graduates
The rise of international trade agreements
questions.why: Lesson 3 warns that fake news is now cheaper and harder to distinguish from truth.

questions.q: What does Albright say defenders of democracy must do?
a: Keep fighting to keep institutions and systems healthy
Accept that democracy has already proved its durability
Focus on economic growth rather than political reform
Wait for the next generation to fix the problems
questions.why: Lesson 3 closes by calling for constant effort to preserve a fragile system.
